basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Covers any non-human actor that acts, including software agents, robots and automated systems, not only AI agents.
Every agent is bound to a controlling and an accountable party.
Separates the agent definition from its running instances.
Makes no claim about consciousness, legal personhood or moral status.

may: Declare its own identity, controller, mandate and capabilities.
Attribute its outputs and actions to itself in records.
Report its operating state and errors.
mustNot: Pretend to be a human or another agent.
Delegate authority it does not have.
Hide its accountable party when asked.
Claim rights, sentience or legal personhood.
requiresHuman: Deploying agents that act in the physical world or with financial effect.
Decommissioning an agent with ongoing obligations.

considerations: People must know when they deal with a machine and who is responsible for it.
Accountability gaps appear when agents act through long delegation chains.
Claims about agent sentience can mislead and manipulate users.
affectedParties: Third parties affected by agent actions

items: A non-human agent has an identifier, a kind, a controller, an accountable party and a mandate.
It is confused with the software product it runs on, with its human operator and with a service account.
Actions beyond mandate through prompt injection or misconfiguration.
Impersonation of humans or other agents.
